pending.title: Fluorite solubility in Na-K-Cl-SO4 aqueous solutions at elevated temperatures and pressures: Experimental constraints and thermodynamic modeling
pending.authors: Wei Zhang, Xiaoqing Song, Qihai Shu et al.
pending.abstract: Fluorite solubility in hydrothermal fluids plays an important role in fluorite mineralization and fluoride transport, yet reliable thermodynamic models at elevated temperatures and pressures remain limited. Here, we developed a Pitzer-based thermodynamic model for fluorite solubility in Na-K-Cl-SO 4 -bearing aqueous solutions at temperatures up to 260 °C and pressures up to 500 bar. The model incorporates pressure-dependent interaction parameters constrained by solution density, solubility, and electromotive force measurements. Its predictions agree well with independent fluorite solubility measurements in KCl solutions at 250 °C and elevated pressure. Model calculations show that increasing pressure generally enhances fluorite solubility in KCl solutions, whereas its effect in NaCl solutions depends on both salinity and temperature and can reverse at higher salinities. Under the modeled high-salinity NaCl conditions, cooling can reduce solubility more strongly than decompression. Reactions between fluoride-bearing fluids and anhydrite promote fluorite precipitation by supplying Ca 2+ , depleting dissolved fluoride while releasing sulfate. This ligand redistribution could sustain metal transport through sulfate complexation despite fluoride remove. The model provides a thermodynamic framework for evaluating how fluid evolution and mineral–fluid reactions control fluorite precipitation and fluoride–sulfate redistribution.

pending.authors: Yongliang Chen, Jifeng Yang
pending.abstract: Mineral prospectivity modeling (MPM) utilizing geochemical and geophysical big data is frequently compromised by spatial autocorrelation, extreme class imbalance, and limited model interpretability. To address these challenges, a spatially constrained programmable photonic deep extreme learning machine (PP‑DELM) is proposed. The PP‑DELM integrates residual connections, batch normalization, and ensemble early stopping to facilitate rapid, robust, and physically informed training. Spatial dependence and information leakage are mitigated through a combined strategy: either K–means clustering–based blocking or label–driven adaptive latitudinal blocking for spatial partitioning, intra–fold reliable negative filtering for label contamination control, and inter–block spatial buffer isolation for cross–block leakage suppression. Model hyperparameters are tuned by combining K–means clustering–based spatial block cross–validation with adaptive Bayesian optimization via a composite objective that prioritizes metrics sensitive to rare positive events. The model’s extrapolative predictive performance is evaluated using label–driven adaptive latitudinal blocking cross–validation. Validated on a multi–feature dataset (14 geochemical and 4 geophysical variables) across 173,362 grid cells in the Langshan–Zhaertai metallogenic belt, Inner Mongolia, China, the PP–DELM achieves performance superior to conventional DELM, Support Vector Machine, and non–negative Positive–Unlabeled (nnPU) learning across metrics including recall@5% and success rate. pending.authors: Yan Ning, Yongzhi Wang, Jiangtao Tian et al.
pending.abstract: Mineral prospectivity mapping helps explorers prioritize decision making capacity in exploration. Recently, deep learning methods have been widely applied because they can automatically learn the nonlinear characteristics of data. However, they have some limitations, making it difficult to explicitly incorporate metallogenic processes. This study uses metallogenic system to guide the formulation of prediction tasks and proposes a novel deep learning method for mineral prospectivity mapping based on a three-branch attention mechanism. This method extracts the sequence features, channel features, and global features around the central sample through a three-branch attention mechanism, thereby effectively exploring its surrounding local pattern information. Specifically, the sequence attention mechanism captures the relationships between sequences. The channel attention mechanism assigns adaptive weights to different channels. The global attention mechanism focuses on the entire data space to capture the complex relationships across different dimensions. Finally, a multi-scale convolutional neural network is employed to extract and fuse data features, which is then combined with a multi-layer perceptron to complete the corresponding prediction tasks. pending.authors: Zhenzhen Li, Kezhang Qin, Shane Webb et al.
pending.abstract: The Chalukou deposit, located in the northern Great Xing’an Range, Northeast China, is one of the largest porphyry Mo deposits globally (2.46 Mt Mo @ 0.087%). This deposit is comprised of a central ore-forming aplite porphyry overprinted successively by silicic, potassic, phyllic, intermediate argillic and weak propylitic zones. White mica occurs in minor amounts in the silicic and inner potassic alteration zones and is abundant in the other alteration zones. In this study, systematic shortwave infrared (SWIR) spectroscopy and electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) were performed to evaluate the effectiveness of white mica spectral parameters as exploration indicators in porphyry Mo deposits. The distinctly higher Pos2200 values in the phyllic zone compared with the intermediate argillic zone are probably driven by changes in fluid pH and temperature. pending.authors: Li Jianlong, Longhui Wang, Weihong Gao et al.
pending.abstract: Rock color zoning is widely used as a redox proxy in sandstone-hosted uranium exploration, but depositional heterogeneity and later fluid overprinting may decouple present-day color from ore-stage redox conditions. We analyzed 16 sandstone samples from borehole ZKY16-32 in the Lower Cretaceous Huanhe Formation, northwestern Ordos Basin, using colorimetry, whole-rock geochemistry, automated mineralogy, and electron probe microanalysis (EPMA). The core contains green, greenish-brown, red, and grayish-green intervals. pending.authors: Cong Li, Wenchang Li, Yu Miao et al.
pending.abstract: The Youjiang Basin hosts the world’s second-largest concentration of Carlin-type gold deposits; however, the source and dynamic evolutionary mechanism of its ore-forming fluids have long remained controversial. The Dixu and Bieli gold deposits in the south-central basin are spatially adjacent and are both hosted in Late Permian tuffs, yet their mineralization ages are constrained to the Late Triassic and Late Jurassic − Early Cretaceous, respectively. This unique phenomenon of “same host strata, different mineralization ages” provides an ideal natural laboratory to investigate fluid evolution under contrasting tectonic regimes. This study systematically compares and constrains the origins of ore-forming fluids for the two deposits and two episodes of regional Carlin-type mineralization by integrating fluid inclusion microthermometry, laser Raman spectroscopy, in-situ LA-ICP-MS microanalysis of individual fluid inclusions, and C-H-O isotope geochemistry. pending.authors: Shengmiao Tong, Guanglai Li, Huaifeng Zhang et al.
pending.abstract: The Garnet Valley deposit in the Damara Orogenic Belt of Namibia hosts both alaskite-hosted and skarn-hosted uranium mineralization, forming a distinctive uranium metallogenic system. This study integrates systematic field investigations with scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), and laser ablation–inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) analyses to investigate the mineralogy, geochemistry, and geochronology of the two mineralization types and to elucidate their genetic relationships. pending.authors: Bin Liu, Weifeng Chen, Dehai Wu et al.
pending.abstract: The Xiwang uranium deposit, located within the Xiazhuang ore field of South China, provides a well-constrained case study of uranium mineralization associated with granitic rocks. In this deposit, pyrite is commonly spatially and texturally associated with pitchblende. In contrast, U-W anomalies are mainly concentrated along pyrite rims, fractures, and zoning boundaries. pending.title: Deciphering controls on variable enrichments of critical metals in IOCG systems by using trace elements of Fe-oxides: A machine learning-based approach
pending.authors: Silin Zhuang, Wei Terry Chen, Xiao-Wen Huang et al.
pending.abstract: Iron Oxide Copper-Gold (IOCG) deposits are generally characterized by variable enrichments/mineralization of critical metals such as Co and REEs, but the controls behind such features are currently poorly understood. This study collected > 1300 trace elemental data of Fe-oxides (magnetite/hematite) from 15 IOCG deposits worldwide to decipher the potential controls through an advanced machine learning-based approach. The selected deposits are variably enriched in Co and REEs in addition to the Fe and Cu mineralization, and were able to be classified as Fe-Cu, Fe-Cu-Co, Fe-Cu-REE and Fe-Cu-Co-REE types. The reprocessed results show that trace elements in Fe-oxides are able to efficiently discriminate the abovementioned four types of IOCGs, and thus can be used as vectors for critical metal enrichments in IOCG systems. A composite machine learning model and a multi-element discriminant diagram, lg(Sn) + lg(Nb) + lg(Mn) versus lg(Co) + lg(V) + lg(Ca), were further proposed to effectively evaluate the potential of Co or REE mineralization in specific deposits. The results also show that the Fe-oxides from Fe-Cu-Co and Fe-Cu-REE ones are broadly relatively enriched in Co or REEs, respectively. This feature indicates that enrichments of REE or Co in IOCG deposits were initially controlled by early Fe mineralizing fluids, but the metals are likely sourced from original magmatic fluids (for the Fe mineralization) or from various hosting rocks through metal mobilization. This study highlights that machine-learning approach on numerical chemical data of common minerals is an efficient tool to discriminate and evaluate potential enrichments of critical metals in IOCG deposits, which is perspective for exploration.

pending.authors: Keqin Tao, Jun Yan
pending.abstract: Mechanisms governing hydrothermal tungsten precipitation, including cooling, boiling, fluid mixing and fluid-rock interaction, represent longstanding controversial issues in economic geology. Herein, six genetically distinct titanite types from the Xiaoyao skarn-type tungsten deposit were investigated to reconstruct the complete magmatic-hydrothermal evolutionary history of the deposit. These types include primary magmatic titanite (Ttn-M) in fresh granodiorite; altered granitic titanite (Ttn-A) in altered granodiorite; as well as prograde skarn titanite (Ttn-P), early oxide-stage titanite (Ttn-O1), late oxide-stage titanite (Ttn-O2), and carbonate–sulfide-stage titanite (Ttn-C) hosted in skarn. In situ EPMA and LA-ICP-MS analyses reveal systematic compositional variations across all titanite populations. Ttn-M exhibits elevated W concentrations compared with that of W-barren granites, indicative of early pre-enrichment in the parental magma before hydrothermal exsolution. Ttn-A, Ttn-P and Ttn-O1 feature extremely high W, reflecting robust tungsten migration from residual magma into hydrothermal fluids and subsequent transport toward skarn. Abrupt W depletion in Ttn-O2 corresponds to large-scale scheelite precipitation. This process elevates fluid pH and promotes the depolymerization of aqueous polytungstate species, thereby facilitating intensive scheelite precipitation. pending.authors: Yihang Gao, Yan Liu
pending.abstract: Carbonatite-related rare earth elements (REE) deposits are the primary global source of light rare earth elements (LREE) resources. All known giant to supergiant carbonatite-related REE deposits show extreme LREE enrichment and relative heavy rare earth elements (HREE) depletion; however, the mechanism of LREE/HREE fractionation during the formation, evolution, and mineralization of carbonatitic magmas remains unclear. The Maoniuping REE deposit, located in the Cenozoic Mianning–Dechang (MD) REE metallogenic belt in southwestern China, is an ideal target for investigating this fractionation process owing to its young mineralization age, relatively weak post-mineralization modification, and well-preserved complete alteration zoning. This study integrates published whole-rock and mineral geochemical data for syenite, carbonatite, and alteration selvages from the Maoniuping deposit, together with new in situ trace element analyses of calcite from REE-mineralized carbonatite and phlogopite from the selvages. Specifically, whole-rock comparisons reveal that syenite shows limited LREE/HREE fractionation (mean LREE/HREE ≈ 62), whereas alteration selvages have similar LREE/HREE ratios (mean LREE/HREE ≈ 58) but markedly elevated total REE contents (mean REE ≈ 4225 ppm); in contrast, REE-mineralized carbonatite exhibit extreme LREE enrichment (mean LREE/HREE ≈ 310) and high total REE contents (mean REE ≈ 8.78 wt%). pending.title: Lithospheric step steepness controls magmatic Ni–Cu sulfide potential at craton margins
pending.authors: Li Liang, He Lanfang, Chen Lin et al.
pending.abstract: Craton margins host most global magmatic Ni–Cu sulfide deposits; however, the controlling mechanisms remain largely equivocal, with no quantitative geodynamic model available to assess the metallogenic potential of different margins. In this study, we develop a first-order metallogenic model that integrates melting thermodynamics, two-phase flow theory, and chalcophile element geochemistry, with lithospheric thickness variation as the primary parameter. The model yields a simple geometric index, the step steepness Δh/L t , where Δh represents the lithospheric thickness contrast between the craton and adjacent mobile belts, and L t represents the transition zone width. A comprehensive fertility index Π is defined, which is proportional to the focused melt flux and metal enrichment efficiency. A steep lithospheric step (large Δh/L t ) raises efficient melt channeling necessary for the formation of giant deposits. The model is evaluated using six well-documented examples, including Norilsk (steep, giant), Jinchuan (steep, giant), Voisey’s Bay (steep, giant), Kingash on the southern margin of the Siberian Craton (gentle, large), Hongqiling (gentle, medium), and the Huangshandong deposit on the northeastern margin of the Tarim Craton (gentle, large). The results are consistent with the model predictions. This study provides a quantitative framework for understanding magmatic sulfide mineralization along craton margins.

pending.title: Chlorite short-wave infrared spectral and mineral-chemical constraints on mineralization in the Haopinggou Au–Ag polymetallic deposit, Xiong’ershan region, China
pending.authors: Li Jiang, Wei Jian, Jingwen Mao et al.
pending.abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) spectroscopy is widely used in hydrothermal mineral exploration; however, chlorite has been less widely applied because its low reflectance, compositional variability, and intergrowth with carbonates complicate spectral interpretation. The relationships among chlorite SWIR parameters, mineral chemistry, and mineralization in hydrothermal ore deposits therefore remain poorly constrained. This study integrates drill-core SWIR spectroscopy, petrographic observations, and electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) to characterize hydrothermal chlorite from the Haopinggou Au–Ag–Pb–Zn polymetallic deposit in the Xiong’ershan district, China. Two chlorite generations are recognized: early Chl-I, occurring mainly as coarse aggregates in weakly mineralized zones, and mineralization-related Chl-II, which is finer grained, sulfide-associated, and compositionally more Fe-rich. EPMA data show that Chl-II has higher FeO contents, Fe 2+ contents, and Fe/(Fe + Mg) ratios than Chl-I, whereas corrected chlorite geothermometry yields overlapping intermediate-temperature estimates of 220–290°C, mostly concentrated between 240 and 280°C. Au-mineralized intervals are characterized by relatively long-wavelength Fe–OH absorption-band positions near 2250 nm (Pos2250), commonly ≥2255 nm, and low ratios of the continuum-removed absorption depth near 2350 nm (Dep2350) to that near 2250 nm (Dep2250), commonly ≤ 1.0. The systematic Fe enrichment of mineralization-related chlorite, together with its characteristic SWIR response, is consistent with relatively reducing hydrothermal conditions associated with Au mineralization. These spectral–mineralogical criteria provide rapid vectors for concealed porphyry-related subepithermal Au–Ag–Pb–Zn mineralization.

pending.abstract: Deciphering how rare metals are transferred from magmatic enrichment to hydrothermal mineralization is essential for understanding granite-related rare-metal ore systems. In this study, we investigate the Cuonadong Sn–W polymetallic deposit by integrating in situ wolframite U–Pb dating, in situ fluorite trace-element analysis, fluid-inclusion microthermometry, and H–O–Sr–Nd–Pb isotope geochemistry, with the aim of reconstructing fluid evolution and its controls on Sn–W mineralization in a fluorine-rich magmatic–hydrothermal system. Wolframite U–Pb age is 14.8 ± 0.6 Ma, broadly coeval with the emplacement of highly fractionated leucogranites and pegmatites, establishing a genetic link between mineralization and late-stage, highly evolved granitic magmatism. pending.authors: Xin Zhang, Xiao-Wen Huang, Yu-Miao Meng et al.
pending.abstract: Geochemical prospectivity mapping in polymetallic districts is often constrained by overlapping geochemical responses, nonlinear multielement relationships, and limited labeled data. Using 233,332 soil geochemical samples for 19 elements from western Guizhou, China, this study develops a modified unsupervised self-organizing map (SOM) workflow. The workflow integrates cluster-number evaluation, hierarchical clustering of component planes for element selection, quantization error (QE), density-based clustering (DBSCAN), and robust Mahalanobis distance (RMD), linking element associations with anomaly-type discrimination and continuous intensity mapping. The workflow was applied to three contrasting metallogenic settings. In the Zn-Pb district of NW Guizhou, cluster-number and input-element optimization improve anomaly focusing and resolve core-to-periphery zonation, while DBSCAN distinguishes Zn-Pb-related anomalies from overlapping Au-related responses. In the Au district of SW Guizhou, the workflow identifies Au-associated anomalies along major faults using available pathfinder elements despite the absence of Au, Sb, and Ag measurements. In the Bijie-Zunyi Ni-Mo-P belt, QE and RMD enhance the expression of weak anomalies and delineate a ring-like pattern spatially associated with mapped folds. Across the three cases, the highest-ranked RMD zones covering 15% of each effective study area capture 82.9–92.1% of known target occurrences, with higher target capture and lower spatial fragmentation than maps based on principal component analysis reconstruction error at the same coverage. pending.authors: Mahnaz Mahboobi, Homayoon Katibeh, Yousef Bahrami et al.
pending.abstract: Accurate, spatially coherent delineation of geochemical anomalies is critical for effective targeting of porphyry copper systems, yet this task is complicated by nonlinear, multivariate and overlapping elemental signatures, as well as the multi‑scale nature of hydrothermal alteration halos. This study introduces a novel, fully unsupervised workflow, UMAP–Hypergraph–Kmeans (UHK), that combines nonlinear manifold learning, higher-order relational modeling, and principled clustering diagnostics to produce compact, geologically coherent anomaly maps. High-dimensional geochemical data were projected with UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) after an exhaustive hyperparameter search (optimal: n_neighbors = 5, min_dist = 0.1; composite score = 0.741), then encoded as a hypergraph to capture multi-sample affinities and suppress spurious pairwise links. Spectral diagnostics of the hypergraph Laplacian guided dimensionality selection and the enriched latent coordinates were partitioned with K-Means (K = 7), yielding clusters with strong cohesion (Silhouette ≈ 0.74) and clear geological interpretability. pending.abstract: Rare metals are becoming increasingly important in the modern world due to their irreplaceable roles in strategic sectors and are largely extracted from highly evolved granites or pegmatites. Nevertheless, the precise mechanisms governing their enrichment remain poorly constrained. The Murong deposit, located in southwestern China, reserves abundant Li-Ta-Nb-(Be-Sn) resources within LCT (Li-Cs-Ta) pegmatites and adjacent altered wall rocks, making it an ideal natural laboratory for investigating enrichment processes. Two stages of hydrothermal fluids exsolved from the melt successively metasomatized adjacent schist. The first-stage fluid exsolved prior to crystallization of magma extracted substantial B and minor Li, Rb, Cs, and Sn from the melt into the schist. Meanwhile, the escape of early fluid elevated the viscosity of the melt and prolonged the nucleation delay, contributing to a favorable environment for the saturation of rare metal minerals. Subsequently, fractional crystallization promoted the enrichment of Rb, Cs, W, Sn, Nb, and Ta, and induced Nb-Ta fractionation, but concurrently led to depletion of Li and Be in the residual melt. Eventually, the second-stage F- and Cl-rich fluid exsolved from the late melt is enriched in rare metals and overprinted adjacent altered schist. During this second-stage fluid exsolution, rare-metal enrichment was mainly controlled by two pathways: direct extraction from the melt for elements with high fluid affinities (Rb, Cs, Sn, W), and efficient leaching from previously crystallized minerals for Li, Be, Nb, and Ta. This late fluid also drove further Nb–Ta fractionation and promoted the precipitation of Ta‑rich phases, underscoring its pivotal role in final ore upgrading. pending.authors: Haoxiang Da, Zhiqiang Wang, Meijuan Zhou et al.
pending.abstract: Extensively fractionated granitoids are exhibit an intrinsic genetic association with rare-metal mineralization events, but the mechanisms for their unusual geochemical features (e.g., low Nb/Ta ratios) and pronounced enrichment of rare metals remain contentious. The existence and role of exsolved fluids are key issues of debate. In this study, we employ biotite as a robust tracer to constrain the magmatic‑hydrothermal transition of the Mesozoic Fuling pluton in the eastern Jiangnan Orogenic Belt. The Fuling pluton consists of coarse-grained biotite monzogranite-syenogranite, medium-fine-grained porphyritic biotite syenogranite and fine-grained biotite syenogranite, in which biotites are classified as BT-I, BT-II and BT-III, respectively. BT-I show high TiO 2 , MgO, Cl, V and Ba and low rare-metal contents. Petrographic observations, whole-rock geochemistry and geochemical modeling collectively reveal that fractional crystallization dominates the compositional evolution of BT‑I biotite. In contrast, BT-III show very low TiO 2 , MgO, Cl, V and Ba and extremely high rare-metal contents, which fails to be adequately accounted for fractional crystallization processes because the required crystallinity is too high (>95 %). Furthermore, we use the difference in fluid mobility of compatible elements (Sc and Mn versus V and Ba) to distinguish hydrothermal from magmatic processes, which unequivocally indicate that BT-III was formed mainly from the entrapped exsolved fluids. pending.title: Magmatic controls on Late Mesozoic large-scale Au-Cu-W-Sn mineralization in southeastern China
pending.authors: Pei Ni, Wensheng Li, Genwen He et al.
pending.abstract: Southeast China represents a major Late Mesozoic polymetallic metallogenic province, hosting several large sized Au–Cu deposits and showing W–Sn mineralization potentials. However, the tectono-magmatic controls of Au–Cu–W–Sn polymetallic mineralization remain highly debated. This study integrates systematic geochronological, petrological, and geochemical data from representative ore deposits in the Qinhang belt, the Wuyi belt, and the coastal region of Southeast China. The Au–Cu mineralization occurred in three pulses: Middle Jurassic (175–165 Ma), Late Jurassic (160–150 Ma), and late Early Cretaceous (110–100 Ma), in response to the initial subduction, continuous subduction, and rollback of the Paleo-Pacific Plate. The 160–150 Ma Dehua system developed in a continental arc setting and hosts numerous epithermal Au–Ag polymetallic deposits. By contrast, both the giant Dexing (170 Ma) and Zijinshan Au–Cu clusters (110 Ma) are suggested to be products of crustal reworking in an intraplate environment or a back-arc setting. Moreover, a major Early Cretaceous (∼135 Ma) W-Sn mineralization event, previously reported in numerous individual studies but rarely integrated into a regional framework, is systematically reviewed and re-evaluated here for the western Wuyi belt, which represents a highly prospective target. Furthermore, epithermal Pb-Zn-Ag activity in the coastal belt has generated substantial by-product enrichment of dispersed metals, particularly Cd. We stress that unlike classic porphyry–epithermal systems in arc settings, the large-scale Au–Cu–W–Sn mineralization in back-arc or intracontinental settings in Southeast China was primarily derived from crustal reworking.

Eight oxide components (WO 3 , Nb 2 O 5 , Ta 2 O 5 , TiO 2 , SnO 2 , Sc 2 O 3 , FeO, and MnO) were selected as input variables based on their geological relevance and analytical consistency. Four classification algorithms, including random forest (RF), XGBoost, decision tree (DT), and support vector machine (SVM), were optimized and compared. The optimized RF model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 92.73 % and an ROC-AUC value of 0.993. SHAP-based interpretation demonstrates that the model predictions are controlled by multi-element associations rather than individual elemental thresholds. pending.authors: Nikolai Nekrylov, Christian A. Bergemann, Samvel Hovakimyan et al.
pending.abstract: Iron oxide–apatite (IOA) deposits are globally significant sources of Fe, P, and Rare Earth Elements (REEs). Although input of hydrothermal processes into their origin is acknowledged, direct temporal constraints on the duration and style of their hydrothermal evolution remain scarce. The Abovyan deposit in central Armenia, hosted by late Miocene andesites, is one of the youngest known IOA systems worldwide and the only example in the Lesser Caucasus, providing a rare opportunity to address this problem. We integrate in-situ U–Pb dating of apatite and monazite with electron microprobe and LA-ICP-MS analyses, Raman spectroscopy and textural observations on samples from a single continuous drill core (67–337 m). A total of 162 analyses define a narrow age window between 5.58 ± 0.08 and 4.98 ± 0.07 Ma. Pristine F-rich apatite from the top and base of the section yields the oldest ages, consistent with magmatic crystallization. Monazite confined to Cl-bearing apatite domains gives an intermediate age of 5.26 ± 0.06 Ma, demonstrating new hydrothermal crystallization. Younger ages in Cl-rich, inclusion-rich apatite of the upper–middle interval extend down to 4.98 ± 0.07 Ma and provide direct evidence that hydrothermal activity continued after monazite formation. The depth-dependent spread of apatite ages is a record of staged fluid–rock interaction. Incomplete replacement of early F-rich apatite by later Cl-rich generations is reflected in younger apparent (mixed) ages, which document a minimum duration of hydrothermal activity in the upper-middle part of the deposit for at least several hundred thousand years after magmatic crystallization. papers.authors: Jinhua Qin, Yan Wang, Liu Shanbao et al.
papers.abstract: Complex Intrusive-volcanic systems, critical reservoirs for porphyry and subvolcanic hydrothermal Sn deposits, have been a subject of great controversy regarding whether intrusion or volcanic events could effectively contribute to significant Sn mineralization. We address this issue through detailed field work, ore mineralogy, mineral geochemistry, and cassiterite U–Pb geochronology of the Taoxiba Sn deposit. Three metallogenic stages and seven generations of cassiterite have been identified: cassiterite Cst-G occurs in greisen, cassiterite Cst-W1–4 occur in altered volcanic rocks, and cassiterite Cst-V1 & V2 occur exclusively in mica-quartz veins. Each cassiterite generation showing distinct trace-element compositions. The Nb, Ta, and Sc accumulated in the Cst-G generations are derived from the inherited concentrations of Nb and Ta from the initial magma and absorbed through the mechanisms of Sc 3+ + (Nb 5+ , Ta 5+ ) ↔ 2Sn 4+ and Fe 2+ /Mn 2+ + 2Nb 5+ /Ta 5+ ↔ 3Sn 4+ . However, the Cst-W1–W4 and Cst-V1 generations followed the Fe 3+ + Nb 5+ /Ta 5+ ↔ 2Sn 4+ mechanism. The high Pb, Th, and ∑REE concentrations in are possibly originated from fluid-rock interactions, fluid mixing, differential partitioning, or fluid boiling, among other processes. However, the abnormal Fe, Ti, Hf, Zr, Ga, Be, and Mn concentrations in Cst-W4 record complex mixing of externally derived fluids in a distal open low-temperature system. The Taoxiba magmatic–hydrothermal system experienced at least three evolutionary stages: a high-temperature, reduced greisen stage; a subsequent cooling and oxidation stage; and a later overprinting stage involving externally derived hydrothermal fluids. papers.title: Geochemistry and platinum-group mineralogy of chromitites and the limonite zone from the Santa Cruz Ni-laterite deposit, Acoje, Philippines
papers.authors: Matías García-Tudela, Thomas Aiglsperger, Diego Domínguez-Carretero et al.
papers.abstract: The Santa Cruz Ni-laterite deposit, developed over the upper mantle section of the Acoje Ophiolite Block, provides a natural setting to investigate platinum-group element (PGE) and platinum-group mineral (PGM) behavior during serpentinization and lateritization of chromitites and their host peridotites. We studied dunite-hosted chromitites, laterite-hosted chromitites, and samples from the limonite zone. Despite hydrothermal and supergene overprints, all chromitites retain a magmatic signature typical of high-Cr ophiolitic chromitites (Cr# > 0.6). Trace-element patterns and calculated parental melts confirm crystallization from boninite-like melts during subduction initiation in a fore-arc setting. Laterite-hosted chromitites are Ir-group PGE (IPGE: Os, Ir, Ru)-enriched and contain Ru-Os-Ir-rich PGM enclosed within, or along the margins of, chromite, recording magmatic precipitation before or during chromite crystallization. In contrast, dunite-hosted chromitites are Pd-group PGE (PPGE: Rh, Pt, Pd)-enriched and contain Pt-Pd-rich PGM associated with interstitial base-metal sulfides, reflecting immiscible sulfide melt(s) segregation after chromite crystallization. These observations suggest that dunite-hosted chromitites are not the bedrock source of laterite-hosted chromitites; rather, both are distinct occurrences that crystallized at different stages during boninitic-like melt evolution. Serpentinization locally modified exposed PGM and sulfides and promoted secondary PGM formation. papers.title: From metasedimentary rocks to evolved pegmatitic melts: Tourmaline geochemistry and the origin of Nb-Ta mineralization in the Mufushan area, South China
papers.authors: Nuerkanati Madayipu, Huan Li, Thomas J. Algeo et al.
papers.abstract: The Mufushan region in the South China Jiangnan Orogenic Belt hosts significant rare-metal mineralization, yet the sources of fluids and metals for its pegmatite-hosted Nb-Ta deposit have remained unclear. This study employs tourmaline, an accessory mineral throughout the deposit, to trace Nb-Ta variations in the melt or fluid. Integrated textural and geochemical analyses of tourmaline from slate, schist, granite, ore-bearing pegmatite, and ore-free pegmatite reveal that all tourmalines belong to the alkali group (predominantly schorlitic, hydroxy species), with substitutions governed by (Fe 2+ Fe 3+ )(MgAl) −1 and AlO[R(OH)] −1 vectors, defining a foitite to magnesio-foitite trend. Tourmalines from metasedimentary rocks are Mg-rich, whereas those from granite and pegmatites are Fe-rich, with high Fe/(Mg+Fe) ratios (0.61–0.74) in the latter. Metasedimentary-hosted tourmalines show elevated Sr, Sc, Ni, and V, indicating host-rock control. Ore-bearing pegmatite tourmalines record melt evolution with progressive Nb, Li, and Cs enrichment, distinct from Be-enriched ore-free pegmatite. Boron isotope values (−15.30‰ to −9.54‰, excluding one anomalous slate-hosted outlier at −4.19‰) point to mixed granite and metasedimentary boron reservoirs. We conclude that the Nb-Ta mineralization originated from an evolved magmatic-hydrothermal melt/fluid enriched in Sr, Sc, V, and Mn, derived from the Mufushan granite batholith, which itself was sourced from the Lengjiaxi metasedimentary Group. Among the granitoids, the most evolved phase, muscovite monzogranite associated with rare-metal pegmatites, is the most promising exploration target.

papers.title: Unveiling the subsurface: deep-penetrating geochemical methods and anomaly mechanisms in the Gobi Desert, China
papers.authors: Chunfang Dong, Bimin Zhang, Zimu Yang et al.
papers.abstract: The Gobi Desert of northwestern China represents a highly prospective yet critically under-explored metallogenic province, where thick, transported overburden and extreme aridity have rendered conventional geochemical surveys largely ineffective. Deep-penetrating geochemistry (DPG) has emerged as a suite of specialized surface methods designed to detect concealed mineralization beneath such exotic cover by targeting mobile forms of ore-forming elements that migrate from depth to the surface. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of DPG applications in the Chinese Gobi Desert, integrating landscape geochemistry, method classification, multi-scale exploration strategies, and element migration mechanisms. We evaluate seven DPG methods grouped by sampling medium into soil-based, gas-based, and plant-based approaches, comparing their principles, key procedures, strengths, and limitations. A scale-dependent framework is synthesized to guide the selection of sampling media, extraction techniques, and survey densities for metallogenic belt, regional, and deposit-scale exploration, subject to local geological and cover conditions. Furthermore, we assess proposed element-migration mechanisms involving groundwater circulation, geogas flow, seismic pumping, electrochemical gradients, capillary action, and plant uptake, considering their applicability across saturated and unsaturated environments. This review establishes a coherent framework for method selection in the Gobi Desert and identifies critical frontiers—including nanoparticle characterization, cross-sphere element behavior, isotopic tracing, and artificial intelligence integration—that will drive the next generation of DPG technology toward precision, efficiency, and standardization for concealed mineral resource

papers.abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) and sulfur (S) isotopes in molybdenite provide critical insights into magmatic–hydrothermal processes and hold growing potential for porphyry Mo exploration. Here, we present integrated δ 98 Mo and δ 34 S datasets for molybdenite from the giant Diyanqinamu porphyry Mo deposit (NE China), where the hydrothermal center (defined by alteration and fluid temperature) is spatially decoupled from the mineralization center (defined by Mo grade). Molybdenite δ 98 Mo values range from –0.87 to 0.26‰ and δ 34 S from 3.3 to 10.2‰, with systematic spatial variations. Strong negative correlations between δ 98 Mo and δ 34 S characterize quartz–molybdenite ores (exploration lines 21 and 61), indicating coupled fractionation during molybdenite precipitation. However, the contrasting behavior of Mo and S isotopes across the deposit demonstrates that integrated δ 98 Mo–δ 34 S analysis provides complementary rather than strictly coupled information. Sulfur isotopes record fluid boiling and fluid–rock reactions, with δ 34 S increasing outward from the hydrothermal center. Molybdenum isotopes are insensitive to these processes and instead reflect precipitation kinetics: rapid, near–quantitative precipitation in distal areas yields restricted δ 98 Mo variability and high Mo grades, whereas slower Rayleigh–dominated precipitation near the hydrothermal center produces wider isotopic variation and lower Mo grades. Quantitative modeling indicates that molybdenite precipitated from sulfur–limited fluids (m S /m Mo = 1.5–2), with only 70–80% of available Mo removed from solution. This interpretation is robust to reasonable uncertainties in fractionation factors, although alternative mechanisms (e.g., boiling‑induced sulfur loss to vapor) cannot be excluded. papers.abstract: Numerous fluorite deposits occur in the Kalaqin district along the northern margin of the North China Craton, yet their timing and genesis remain poorly constrained. Fluid inclusions in fluorite are predominantly liquid-rich and yield a mean homogenization temperature of 160 °C, a mean salinity of 2.64 wt% NaCl equiv., and a mean density of 0.93 g/cm −3 . These data define a low- to moderate-temperature, low-salinity, low-density NaCl–H 2 O system. The H–O isotope compositions (δD = -104.5 ‰ to −81.4 ‰; δ 18 O = -11.3 ‰ to −3.8 ‰) indicate that meteoric water dominated the ore-forming fluids. Fluorite yielded a calibrated U–Pb age of 67.7 ± 2.8 Ma (2σ), constraining the principal mineralization to the latest Cretaceous, broadly coeval with the second phase of slow exhumation at the Anjiayingzi gold deposit (100–65 Ma) and F-bearing hydrothermal alteration at Fengning (63.0 ± 7.3 Ma). The spatial distribution of Group A intrusions is broadly consistent with nearby mineralisation occurrences. These results provide a practical zircon–apatite proxy framework for prioritising intrusions with higher ore-forming potential.

papers.title: Association-dissociation behavior of MgSO4 solution at high temperature and pressure: Constraints from in situ Raman quantitative experiments
papers.authors: Zimeng Li, Richen Zhong, Hao Cui et al.
papers.abstract: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO 4 ) is a major electrolyte in hydrothermal fluids and proposed subsurface oceans on icy planetary bodies. Its association-dissociation behavior controls the concentrations of free SO 4 2− and MgSO 4 (aq) in MgSO 4 solutions, but quantitative constraints at elevated temperature and pressure remain limited. Here, we used fused silica capillary capsule (FSCC) experiments combined with in situ Raman spectroscopy to quantify association-dissociation behavior in a 1.2 m MgSO 4 solution at 24 − 243 °C and pressures up to ∼ 340 MPa. Calibrated Raman data show that free SO 4 2− dominates at low temperature, whereas MgSO 4 (aq) increases with heating and becomes predominant above ∼ 150 °C. In the overlapping 85 − 182 °C interval, two samples followed markedly different pressure paths but yielded the same temperature-dependent speciation trend. No detectable pressure effect on MgSO 4 association-dissociation behavior was observed within uncertainty over this overlapping temperature interval. We further used the Raman-derived speciation data to optimize empirical thermodynamic parameters for MgSO 4 (aq) in the modified Ryzhenko-Bryzgal (RB) model. The parameters reproduce the observed MgSO 4 association trend for the 1.2 m solution within the investigated P − T range. Extrapolation to other concentrations and more complex natural fluids should be made with caution.
papers.summary: Raman measurements at up to 243 °C and about 340 MPa show MgSO4 ion pairing rises with heat and dominates above about 150 °C.

papers.title: Unraveling the hydrothermal evolution and exploration vectors of IOA system in the Xiangshannan-Dadiantang deposit, Ningwu District: Insights from SWIR spectroscopy and mineral chemistry
papers.authors: Wencheng Zhang, Fangyue Wang, Taofa Zhou et al.
papers.abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) spectroscopy is widely applied in hydrothermal exploration but remains limited in IOA systems, where exploration indicators and vectors are poorly constrained. This study examines the Xiangshannan–Dadiantang (X–D) magnetite deposit (Ningwu district, eastern China) using integrated SWIR, EPMA, and LA-ICP-MS analyses to define alteration mineralogy, trace the evolution of magnetite and chlorite, and develop SWIR-based exploration vectors for high-grade iron ore. Four magnetite types (Mag.1–Mag.4) indicate multistage mineralization: disseminated (Mag.1) with albite; massive (Mag.2) as high-grade ore (TFe > 50%) associated with actinolite–apatite; brecciated (Mag.3) affected by chloritization–epidotization; and vein-type (Mag.4) associated with epidote–chlorite at vein margins. LA-ICP-MS data show that Mag.2 is enriched in Mg, Ca, and Zn. Mg-in-magnetite thermometry indicates decreasing formation temperatures from Mag.2 to Mag.4, reflecting progressive cooling. Chlorite exhibits systematic zonation, with Mg enrichment and Fe depletion near high-grade ore zones, along with increasing Ca and decreasing Mn. SWIR spectral parameters show a relatively stable Fe–OH peak position (Pos2250) but a systematic shift of the Mg–OH peak Position (Pos2335) toward shorter wavelengths, together with elevated chlorite IC values (>2) near ore zones. These spectral signatures correlate with Mg-enriched, Fe-depleted chlorite and are interpreted to reflect Fe consumption during magnetite precipitation and Mg input from earlier alteration and hydrothermal fluids. Integrated with mineral chemistry, these results define SWIR-based exploration criteria for X-D IOA deposits and demonstrate the effectiveness of SWIR spectroscopy as a vectoring tool toward high-grade iron ore
papers.summary: Short-wave infrared spectra and chlorite chemistry show that a Mg-OH peak shift and high chlorite IC values point toward high-grade magnetite ore in an iron oxide-apatite system.
papers.deposit_type: Iron oxide-apatite (IOA) magnetite deposit with chlorite alteration vectoring
papers.commodities: Iron (magnetite), with apatite, and trace Mg, Ca, Zn in magnetite
papers.setting: Ningwu volcanic basin, eastern China; Mesozoic intrusion-related iron ore, with alteration of volcanic and intrusive host rock
papers.where_it_applies: Lower 48 IOA districts in the Pea Ridge and Pilot Knob area of Missouri, and the Adirondacks in New York, are the best match. Background: SWIR (portable spectrometer) alteration mapping is routine in both the Lower 48 and Alaska, but the Alaska match for IOA is weak.

papers.title: Sandstone-hosted uranium mineralization in the Lower Cretaceous aeolian red beds: A case study from the Jingchuan deposit in the southwestern Ordos Basin, China
papers.authors: Yin Chen, Michel Cuney, Julien Mercadier et al.
papers.abstract: Sandstone-hosted uranium deposits have been highlighted within the Meso–Cenozoic continental basins of Northern China. The Ordos Basin, in particular, hosts large, prospective deposits in the Lower Cretaceous aeolian sandstones. However, the altered mineral assemblages, paragenetic sequences, and metallogenic mechanisms of these red-bed-hosted deposits remain contentious. papers.title: Y-shaped faults and their control on orogenic gold mineralization: Field survey and particle flow code (PFC) numerical simulation on the Dongkeng deposit in South China
papers.authors: JiaJian LU, Yi Zheng, Xi Chen et al.
papers.abstract: Structural controls play a crucial role in the formation of hydrothermal deposits. Orogenic gold deposits, as a typical structurally controlled ore type, are profoundly influenced by geometry, stress-field evolution, and reactivation of faults. The large Dongkeng orogenic gold deposit, located in the Yunkai Domain, Cathaysia Block, South China, is controlled by a NW-trending brittle-ductile shear zone, which is interpreted as a subordinate fault to the regional NE-trending Wuchuan-Sihui Fault. Together, these faults form a representative Y-shaped fault-controlled ore system. However, how this planar Y-shaped fault system controls the formation of the Dongkeng orogenic gold deposit remains unclear. We conducted a field geological survey to document in detail the characteristics of the ore-controlling structures and related alteration-mineralization. On this basis, we used the Particle Flow Code (PFC) discrete element method to construct a Y-shaped fault model comprising the major and subordinate faults, and simulated the deformation and fracturing processes under compressive, extensional, and alternating stress conditions. Our results indicate that the subordinate fault is more prone to developing interconnected fracture networks than the major fault. Furthermore, an alternating extensional-compressional stress regime may preferentially form interconnected fracture networks that could enhance local permeability, and therefore provide potential channels and places for migration and precipitation of deep ore-forming fluids. Our study highlights that the subordinate fault preferentially localizes large, high-grade gold orebodies, and offers important guidance for exploration.
papers.summary: Field mapping and discrete-element modelling show that the subordinate fault at Dongkeng builds more connected fracture networks, and that alternating stress favours fluid pathways and high-grade gold.
papers.deposit_type: Orogenic gold (brittle-ductile shear-zone hosted)
papers.commodities: Gold
papers.setting: Brittle-ductile shear zone with NW-trending structures and a subordinate fault to the regional NE-trending Wuchuan-Sihui fault; Cathaysia Block, South China
papers.where_it_applies: Alaska's orogenic gold belts, including the Juneau gold belt and the Tintina-related belt of interior Alaska, are a good match, since the structural controls are similar. Lower 48 orogenic gold districts such as the Mother Lode in California and the Carolina slate belt fit the same logic.

papers.title: Lithium cycling in the source-to-sink system of a typical salt lake in the Western Kunlun: multi-isotopic constraints and end-member quantification
papers.authors: Yanji Li, Miao Weiliang, Maoyong He et al.
papers.abstract: The Western Kunlun region of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau is a premier lithium province characterized by the coexistence of super-large pegmatite and brine-type lithium deposits. This spatial association provides a unique laboratory to investigate the lithium cycle from the lithosphere to the hydrosphere. This study utilizes hydrochemistry and a multi-isotope (δ 7 Li、δ 11 B、 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) framework across 50 water samples from the Tianshuihai-Kushui Lake basin to quantify lithium sources and enrichment mechanisms. Results identify three End-members with distinct geochemical fingerprints: springs in the northwest of Kushui Lake (End‑member A), Tianshuihai water system (End‑member B), and Western Kunlun Mountain Rivers (End‑member C). The water–rock interaction during the upwelling of deep fluids is the key process for lithium enrichment in Kushui Lake. Sr isotope binary‑mixing modelling yields a fluid‑volume mixing fraction of 88.6 % for deep‑fluid‑dominated End‑member A; mass‑balance calculation further reveals End‑member A supplies 71.0 % of total dissolved Sr mass and 64.2 % of lithium mass to the system. Supergene lithium enrichment follows a three-stage evolution: evaporation-driven linear accumulation, an adsorption-buffering phase, and terminal-basin selective enrichment. Based on these findings, this study establishes a “mobilization-migration-enrichment” lithium cycle model. This model represents a transition from “endogenous enrichment” in the lithosphere to “exogenous ore formation” in the hydrosphere, this coupled genetic model is likely a common phenomenon in Li-rich salt lakes across the Kunlun orogenic belt on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau.
